content: The Early Warning and Response System (EWARS) for Dengue Outbreaks is a tool designed to assist in the prediction and management of dengue outbreaks. It was developed as part of a collaborative effort led by the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR), in partnership with the World Health Organization (WHO) and other organizations. The system aims to address the challenges posed by late detection and inadequate response mechanisms, which exacerbate the rapid transmission of dengue. The operational guide for EWARS provides program managers with a user-friendly tool that enables them to analyze historical dengue data, identify appropriate alarm indicators for predicting outbreaks, and use these results to build a real-time early warning system. The guide includes step-by-step instructions for organizing raw data, entering it into statistical software, running the software, and interpreting the results. It also includes troubleshooting sections and a technical annex for advanced users who wish to understand the underlying statistical processes and source code. The guide emphasizes the importance of ensuring that surveillance datasets are compatible with the statistical software package, Stata. This includes adhering to specific formatting rules, such as consistent variable names, numeric data storage, and proper column headings. The guide also outlines the installation of necessary Stata packages, such as mkmat and matsave, to facilitate the analysis. The EWARS package comprises four essential files: two do-files, a surveillance dataset, and a surveillance workbook. These files must be stored in the same folder on the user's computer. The do-files serve as platforms for entering commands and running the model in Stata, while the surveillance workbook is an Excel file used for prospective early warning system analysis. The guide provides detailed instructions on preparing the dataset, including the inclusion of general variables (e.g., year, epidemiological week, population size), outbreak indicators (e.g., weekly hospitalized cases), and alarm indicators (e.g., mean humidity, weekly rainfall, mean temperature). Users are advised to ensure consistency in variable names and formats across all datasets. The EWARS system was developed as part of a European Union-funded research program, the International Research Consortium on Dengue Risk Assessment, Management, and Surveillance (IDAMS). It aims to build technical capacity and provide a standardized methodology for predicting dengue outbreaks in resource-constrained settings. The guide was authored by Laith Hussain-Alkhateeb, Leigh Bowman, and Max Petzold, with contributions from various experts and beta testers. The system's ultimate goal is to enhance the ability of countries to predict and respond to dengue outbreaks effectively, thereby reducing the burden of this disease on national health systems.
